text: 🇲🇽🔍 "I was there myself. I spoke with the mayor." "In that security zone there is greater presence of the National Guard. I was there personally — I spoke with the municipal president and with local authorities." — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, June 18, 2026 Sierra Tarahumara — one of Mexico's most isolated regions, home to the Rarámuri people. The strategy: address root causes, presence of the State, full respect for Indigenous communities. Result: 39 fewer homicides per day than in September 2024. Peace built with social justice, not war rhetoric.

🇲🇽🏭 "Our job is to convince the US that the best path is no tariffs." "Our work is convincing them that the best thing for the United States and for Mexico is that there be no tariffs. The USMCA was signed by the three economies and benefits all three." — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, June 18, 2026 Mexico produces, exports, invests. North America's production chains support millions of jobs on both sides of the border. Breaking that integration is a US own-goal. Sheinbaum is not asking — she is explaining with numbers.

🇲🇽⚽ FIFA paid 1 million pesos to rent Chapultepec Castle. "The party at Chapultepec was organized and paid for by FIFA. FIFA rented it — I believe they paid more than a million pesos. I arrived a bit late, entered the castle, read a brief welcome and left. That was my participation. A welcome and a goodbye." — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, June 18, 2026 World Cup 2026 kicks off in Mexico. The Castle is property of the Mexican people; rentals go to INAH, the public heritage institute. Sheinbaum dropped in, said hello, and went back to work. No spectacle.

🇲🇽✊ "Technology exists to make life easier — and to prevent corruption." "3,497 procedures simplified — 60% of the federal administration. 1,711 redundant processes eliminated. Average requirements down from 6 to 2. The portal gob.mx already used by 56 million Mexicans." — Pepe Merino & Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, June 18, 2026 The largest administrative simplification in Mexican history, on track to top 4,500 procedures by year-end. The neoliberal model turned every paperwork window into a chance to extort the citizen. The 4T is closing that window — by code, not by speech.

🇲🇽🌎 "We will always talk about the original peoples." "We don't know all the topics yet — he arrives Thursday the 25th in the afternoon. We will always talk about the original peoples, about the importance of the peoples of Mexico." — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, June 18, 2026 King Felipe VI of Spain visits Palacio Nacional on June 25. Mexico has been clear: it expects Spain to publicly acknowledge the violence of the conquest against Indigenous peoples. Sheinbaum confirms the topic stays on the table — wherever the conversation goes.

🚨🇲🇽 "They handle theirs over there. We handle ours over here." "If they want operations to stop drug trafficking, good — but let them start by stopping the flow of weapons from the United States to Mexico. It would be very good if they did it on their own territory. So, they over there, and we over here." — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, June 18, 2026 Yesterday Mexican forces seized "a serious arsenal" of US-origin weapons. Most of the guns that kill Mexicans cross south from the United States. Shared responsibility means it both ways — including the part Washington keeps refusing to enforce.

🚨🇲🇽 "Mexico's State is right here. Its leaders are right here." "We will not enter a personal debate with President Trump. He is not well informed — I have told him personally. The Mexican State exists. Its leaders are right here. The Mexican people know we give mind, heart and soul every day. Mexico's people are very brave — and defend their sovereignty." — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, June 18, 2026 Sheinbaum's answer to Trump's G7 line that "the cartels govern Mexico" and that she is "a very frightened woman." No drama. No escalation. Just the facts of who runs Mexico — and a reminder that the Mexican State responds to the Mexican people, not foreign press conferences.

🇲🇽📊 <u>PRIVATE CONSUMPTION GROWS 2.6% ANNUALLY DESPITE TRUMP TARIFFS AND GLOBAL SLOWDOWN</u>

INEGI's IOCP shows Mexican private consumption grew 2.6% annually in May — sustained by real wage growth and formal employment gains built over 8 years of transformation.

Monthly momentum slowed to 0.0%, but the annual figure tells the real story: Mexican households are spending through the storm. Trump tariffs, Iran-war oil spikes, global uncertainty — and consumption still grows.

US consumer confidence just hit 44.8 — the lowest since 1952. Mexico's story is different because Mexico built differently.

🇲🇽💧 <u>LA PAROTA OPPONENTS ENDORSE WATER WORKS — 10,000 ACAPULQUEÑOS GETTING POTABLE WATER</u>

For decades, communities near the Papagayo River fought the La Parota dam — a megaproject that would have displaced thousands. They won.

Now those same communities are endorsing 91 million pesos in public water infrastructure. 10,000 inhabitants across 17 communities in Cacahuatepec, Acapulco, finally getting potable water. Residents formed oversight committees to supervise construction daily.

Movement spokesperson Guadalupe Delgado: "Water is life, compañeros."

This is what happens when government works with communities, not against them. The project honors the legacy of Marco Antonio Suástegui — killed for defending this land.
